For three glorious hours, Stereophonic drops its audience into a unique agony: the pursuit of artistic perfection. David Adjimi’s astounding new work, itself near-perfect, captures the wondrous highs and excruciating lows of the creative process with a hilarious, painstaking precision. You’ll want to live in this play forever.
Adjmi captures that claustrophobia and inability to communicate, making his “Stereophonic” one of the very best plays to open last year Off Broadway and now this season on Broadway.

Taken as a whole, this is easily one of my favorite theatre experiences of the year, partially because the lives of audio technicians and sound designers and recording artists are not often addressed except as side characters in a world to which we are integral.
